title: Taking the Stairs Is a Real Workout
hook: In an analysis of more than 480,000 people, regular stair climbers were 39% less likely to die of cardiovascular disease — from a habit that costs nothing and takes no planning.
key_points: Pooled data on 480,000+ people compared habitual stair climbers with people who rarely take stairs.
Stair climbers had 39% lower cardiovascular death risk and 24% lower all-cause death risk.
They also showed lower rates of heart attack, stroke, and heart failure.
Stairs deliver short bursts of vigorous effort, the kind that raises fitness fastest.
This is observational — fitter people take more stairs — but the habit is free to adopt.
content_html: A large analysis pooling data on more than 480,000 people found that the people who habitually take the stairs were 39% less likely to die of cardiovascular disease, and 24% less likely to die of any cause, than people who rarely bother. They also had lower rates of heart attack, stroke, and heart failure.
extra_html:
The appeal here is the price. Stairs require no gym, no gear, and no block of time set aside — they're already in your building, and climbing them is genuinely vigorous work. Short bursts at high intensity are the kind of effort that raises cardiorespiratory fitness fastest, which is probably why such a small habit tracks with such a large difference.

The usual caution applies: this is observational research, and people who are already fit and healthy are more likely to skip the elevator in the first place. Some of the gap reflects that, not the stairs. But it's a rare case where the caveat barely matters — there's no downside to taking the stairs, and no reason to wait for a randomized trial before you start.

related.title: Is 150 Minutes a Week Really Enough?
related.hook: The famous 150-minute target may buy less heart protection than advertised. A large study points to roughly 560–610 minutes a week for substantially bigger gains.

related.title: Move More, Sit Less
related.hook: Even if you hit the gym, hours of unbroken sitting carry their own health risk. Breaking up the day with movement matters as much as the workout.

related.title: How Much Exercise You Actually Need
related.hook: The headline number is smaller than most people fear: about 150 minutes of moderate activity a week — roughly 20-some minutes a day — moves the needle on your health.

choices.text: About 39% less likely to die of cardiovascular disease

flashcards.explanation_html: Across more than 480,000 people, habitual stair climbers had a 39% lower risk of cardiovascular death and 24% lower all-cause death risk.

flashcards.prompt: Why can't this study prove stairs themselves cause the longer life?
flashcards.back_html: It's observational. People who are already fitter and healthier are more likely to choose stairs, so some of the benefit may run in that direction.

flashcards.prompt: What makes stair climbing unusually efficient exercise?
flashcards.back_html: It delivers short bursts of vigorous effort — the intensity that improves fitness fastest — without needing equipment, a gym, or extra time in your day.
